subject: Livestream endpoint: elevated streaming latency — immediate mitigation and playbook
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Livestream endpoint: elevated streaming latency — initial report

Hi Alex,

Quick heads-up — our monitoring picked up increased 95th/99th percentile latency on the livestream/chat streaming endpoint serving ClearWave's production region (us-west-2) starting ~2027-10-18 08:40 PDT. ClearWave reported user-visible delays in conversation updates and occasional multi-second gaps between streamed chunks.

What we have so far:
- Elevated token-to-token latencies measured at edge ~200–800ms above baseline for a subset of requests.
- Root cause (preliminary): an autoscaling imbalance in a routing tier + transient KV-cache miss storms during a configuration rollout.
- Impact window: 08:40–09:05 PDT, still observing intermittent slow tails for a small percentage of sessions.

Attached is a tarball with traces and representative logs for your team to review: support_log_1018.tar.gz

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm whether you saw the same user symptoms (gaps in streaming, delayed chunk arrival)?
2) If you have a short test workspace we can use, we'll coordinate a live test while we apply mitigations.

Short-term mitigation we are applying now (non-disruptive):
- Route new traffic to a warmed routing pool to reduce inter-node handoffs.
- Enable a conservative streaming chunk-size override for affected sessions to reduce KV cache pressure.

I'll loop in Ben and Kim for remediation and a formal post-incident follow-up. Sorry for the interruption — we realize ClearWave is in a live demo window this morning and are prioritizing.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: support_log_1018.tar.gz (tgz, 4.2MB)
From: Alex Moreno <alex@clearwave.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, support@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Livestream endpoint: elevated streaming latency — initial report

Dylan,

We saw exactly that: our support queue logged a spike in reports about delayed messages in the live chat flow around 08:45 PDT. Demo participants noticed long pauses mid-response and sometimes only received the final chunk.

We have a staging token for the demo environment (staging-demo@clearwave) you can use; we can also run synthetic traffic if that helps. Our engineering lead (copied) will be available for a quick handoff.

Two immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share an ETA for a stable mitigation?
- If we need to flip to a backup model or non-streaming fallback, what is the expected UX trade-off?

Appreciate the quick reaction.

—Alex
Head of Product
ClearWave
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Livestream endpoint: elevated streaming latency — remediation plan (internal)

Folks — quick internal runbook while we coordinate with ClearWave: 

1) Short-term mitigations (apply now, low risk):
   - Force-route ClearWave's traffic to the warmed routing pool (routing-tag: cw-warm). This reduces cross-pod routing handoffs.
   - Set runtime stream_chunk_ms to 250ms for their tenant to break up long chunking and reduce KV cache pressure.
   - Temporarily cap concurrent streams per connection for their region to 6 (from 12) to ease burst effects.

2) Medium-term (this afternoon):
   - Roll back the config rollout that introduced a routing weight change (safe rollback tested).
   - Rehydrate KV caches for hot keys used by ClearWave by seeding from snapshot.

3) Fallback options to offer the customer (if symptoms persist):
   - Non-streaming completion endpoint (adds ~300–700ms median latency end-to-end but removes streaming chunking artifacts).
   - Model variant fallback: temporarily switch from rwd-medium-stream to rwd-medium-nostream which is identical model weights but optimized for non-stream decode path.

4) Communication and SLAs:
   - If we exceed the 99.9% streaming availability for more than 1 hour, finance should prepare credit path per contract. Laura, can you prepare a draft credit estimate?

I will own the immediate rollout rollback and routing change. Dylan, can you coordinate the external comms and ask the ClearWave team to run the synthetic tests?

Ben
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Internal note: start incident timeline log in Drive (we'll add more detail after full triage).
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@clearwave.ai>, support@clearwave.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Livestream endpoint: elevated streaming latency — mitigation & test plan

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for the staging token. Quick summary of actions we've taken and what we need from ClearWave to validate:

What we changed (applied at 09:50 PDT):
- Forced your tenant onto warmed routing pool (cw-warm).
- Enabled conservative chunking: stream_chunk_ms=250ms.
- Lowered concurrent streams cap to 6 for your region.

What to validate (your side):
- Please run a short 5-minute synthetic using the staging-demo token and report if you still observe multi-second gaps or missing intermediate chunks.
- If you need to preserve streaming UX during the demo and synthetic indicates improvements, continue with the warmed pool. If issues remain, we recommend switching to the non-streaming endpoint for the demo session — we can do that via a single config flip and keep it open for the duration.

Expected UX trade-offs if you choose non-streaming:
- Responses will arrive as a single completion instead of incremental chunks, so the perceived interactivity is reduced. Median end-to-end latency will typically increase by ~400–600ms, but chunk-stuttering will be eliminated.

Next steps:
- Please run the synthetic test now and reply with results (copy the timestamp).
- Ben will start the safe rollback of the routing config and we will follow with a post-incident timeline and remediation notes.

I've attached a signed acknowledgement document we can use if you prefer an SLA credit path while we finalize the postmortem: sla_commitment_signed.pdf

Best,
Dylan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Livestream endpoint: elevated streaming latency — validation and postmortem request

Dylan / Ben,

We ran the 5-minute synthetic at 10:12 PDT yesterday and saw a marked improvement: chunk delivery was stable and gapped occurrences dropped to near-zero. For the customer-facing demo we kept the warmed routing pool in place and did not switch to non-streaming.

Thank you for the rapid mitigation and clear instructions. Two requests before we close the loop:
1) Please share the post-incident timeline and root cause analysis when available.
2) We would like a short runbook that our engineering on-call can use in future (e.g., when to request warmed routing vs. switch endpoints).

If you can drop the incident report link here, we'll mark the ticket resolved on our side.

—Alex
Head of Product
ClearWave
